This process is a common household practice in the region, reflecting traditional food preservation techniques.

name: Sanchi Pat Manuscript Craft
description: This collection documents the traditional Assamese craft of Sanchi Pat manuscript preparation. The display features essential tools such as grinding stones (sil-pata) used for processing pigments, wooden blocks, and brass containers. The manuscripts themselves are crafted from the processed bark of the Sanchi tree (Aquilaria malaccensis). The traditional waterproof ink, known as mahi, is prepared from a mixture of Silikha seeds, Kehraj grass, ashes, and other herbal components, traditionally applied using bird feather quills. The exhibit includes several framed, finished examples of these historical documents, which are significant to Assamese cultural and literary heritage.

description: Tat Bati is a fundamental traditional warping process in Assamese handloom weaving. This outdoor preparation is a critical step that ensures the threads are properly aligned and tensioned before being transferred to the loom for weaving. It represents a vital, enduring skill within the Assamese textile tradition.

description: Manimuni Xaak (Centella asiatica) is a culturally significant leafy green in Assam, known for its distinct kidney-shaped leaves and fibrous roots. The setup typically includes spiritual offerings such as a lit diya, incense, and symbolic items like books and currency, reflecting the blend of Vedic Brahmanical practices and regional Assamese customs.

It consists of a long, heavy wooden lever balanced on a central fulcrum, with a vertical pestle attached to one end. The pestle rhythmically strikes a mortar embedded in the earthen floor to process grains. Typically housed in a dedicated structure known as a 'Dheki-shal', this implement has been a cornerstone of Assamese domestic life for centuries, predating the Ahom Dynasty. While its usage declined following the introduction of mechanical hullers in the 19th century, it remained a dominant method for rice processing in rural households until the late 20th century. The tool is most actively used during the winter harvest season.

description: The Bihu Dhol is a traditional double-headed drum central to Assamese folk music and the Bihu festival. Its construction features a wooden body and two distinct drum heads made of animal skin, played using a combination of a stick and hand. Historically rooted in the Brahmaputra Valley, the instrument gained royal patronage under the Ahom Dynasty, particularly during the reign of King Rudra Singha. In the 20th century, it evolved into an urban cultural icon in Guwahati, notably following the first public Bihu celebration at Latasil Field in 1931. The asphalt road winds through a scenic landscape characterized by lush greenery, palm trees, and agricultural fields. It serves as a vital local connection, facilitating travel towards Thiruvarur town and the village of Mangudi. The roadside environment features typical rural elements, including traditional thatched-roof huts, utility infrastructure, and agricultural boundaries. The road is actively used by local transport, such as auto-rickshaws, and serves as a primary artery for the surrounding village communities.

name: Mazavarayanallur Village Road Improvement
description: A newly constructed tar road in Mazavarayanallur village, Thiruvarur, developed under the 'Chief Minister's Village Roads Improvement Scheme 2024-2025'. The site features a government project information board on the right, adjacent to a water body with a retaining wall. The left side of the road is bordered by dense trees and a traditional thatched-roof hut, showcasing the blend of rural landscape and modern infrastructure development.

name: Velankanni-Tanjavur Railway Bridge
description: A serene, eye-level view taken from the Mangudi Kudhur Barrage, looking towards the Velankanni-Tanjavur railway bridge. The bridge is a prominent blue-painted steel structure spanning a calm, reflective body of water. The banks are lined with lush, dense green vegetation and trees, creating a natural frame for the bridge. The sky is overcast with soft, diffused light, and the sun's reflection is visible on the water's surface. In the foreground, a stone-paved embankment of the barrage is visible on the right side.

name: Temple Wall Paintings of Thirukkannamangai
description: A series of vibrant, traditional wall paintings located within a temple in Thirukkannamangai, Tamil Nadu. These murals depict various significant scenes from Hindu mythology, with a primary focus on Lord Vishnu and his avatars. Notable compositions include the marriage of Lord Vishnu and Goddess Lakshmi, the Trivikrama (Vamana) avatar, the Samudra Manthan (churning of the ocean), and serene depictions of rishis meditating in natural landscapes. The artwork utilizes a traditional style characterized by vivid colors set against deep blue backgrounds, serving as a visual narrative of religious stories for temple visitors.

keywords_tags: ["Thyagaraja Temple", "Thiruvarur", "Musical Instruments", "South Indian Music", "Temple Heritage", "Museum Display", "Percussion"]
description: A curated museum display case housed within the Thyagaraja Temple in Thiruvarur, dedicated to preserving and showcasing traditional South Indian musical instruments. The exhibit features a variety of percussion and wind instruments, including the Parai, Tappattai, Udukkai, Dolak, Pambai, Nathaswaram, and Mugaveena. Each artifact is mounted against a light blue background and accompanied by bilingual labels (Tamil and English) and specific accession numbers. The display also includes a vinyl record and a comprehensive list of instruments, serving as an educational resource on the musical heritage associated with the temple's rituals and traditions.

name: Bronze Sculptures of the Carnatic Music Trinity
keywords_tags: ["Carnatic Music", "Bronze Sculptures", "Thyagaraja Illam", "Muthuswamy Dikshitar", "Sri Thyagaraja", "Shyama Shastri", "Thiruvarur", "Cultural Heritage"]
description: A set of three bronze sculptures housed at the Thyagaraja Illam in Thiruvarur, depicting the 'Carnatic Music Trinity': Muthuswamy Dikshitar, Sri Thyagaraja, and Shri Shyama Shastri. The figures are depicted in traditional seated postures, adorned with white and gold-bordered dhotis, and each is framed by an intricate circular bronze prabhavali. The statues are displayed on a platform alongside traditional brass oil lamps, with a large framed print of the composers positioned behind them, creating a reverent space dedicated to these foundational figures of South Indian classical music.

The chart features the characters arranged in a grid, with a label indicating the script's historical usage period from 4 A.D. to 9 A.D. The display serves as an informative resource for visitors to understand the evolution of the Tamil script.

keywords_tags: ["Thyagaraja Temple", "Thatta Chutri Mandapam", "Kolam", "Temple Architecture", "Thiruvarur", "Traditional Art", "Stone Carving"]
description: A detailed view of the stone floor within the Thatta Chutri Mandapam at the Thyagaraja Temple in Thiruvarur. The floor features elaborate, hand-drawn kolam patterns incorporating traditional lotus flower motifs. These designs are integral to the temple's daily ritual aesthetics, set against the backdrop of ancient stone pillars.

name: Gajabrishta Vimanam, Thiruvarur
description: The Gajabrishta Vimanam in Thiruvarur is a prime example of traditional Dravidian temple architecture. The term 'Gajabrishta' refers to the unique shape of the vimanam, which resembles the back of an elephant. The structure features a sturdy stone base topped with a brightly painted, ornate superstructure adorned with intricate stucco figures of deities. This architectural style is a hallmark of South Indian temple construction, reflecting deep-rooted cultural and religious traditions.

name: Tiruthandagam Temple Inscription
description: A series of dark stone slabs embedded in the wall of the Arulmigu Thiyaagaraaja Swaamy Temple in Thiruvarur, featuring deeply carved Tamil verses from the Tirumurai, specifically the Tiruthandagam. The inscriptions are organized into numbered sections. A dedication plaque at the base records that the installation was unveiled by A. U. Thandaram Pillai on August 7, 1959, reflecting a mid-20th-century effort to preserve and display sacred literature within the temple complex.

name: Ceiling Paintings at Sufi Shrine, Panagal Road
description: These intricate ceiling paintings are located within a Sufi shrine on Panagal Road, Thiruvarur. The artwork is characterized by highly symmetrical, mandala-like floral motifs, primarily resembling lotus blossoms with layered petals in vibrant orange, blue, and white. Interspersed with these radial designs are geometric grid patterns featuring repeating star-like symbols. The paintings reflect a traditional artistic style, though they currently exhibit signs of aging and weathering, suggesting a need for conservation.

name: Nathaswaram and Thavil Performance at Anjuvattathu Amman Temple
location_text: Anjuvattathu Amman Temple, Kilvelur, Thiruvarur Taluk
keywords_tags: ["Nathaswaram", "Thavil", "Temple Music", "Kilvelur", "Anjuvattathu Amman Temple", "Traditional Music", "South Indian Music"]
description: A traditional musical performance featuring the nathaswaram and thavil, captured in the courtyard of the Anjuvattathu Amman Temple in Kilvelur. The lead musician, dressed in a white shirt and veshti, plays the nathaswaram while seated on the stone floor, accompanied by a thavil player in the background. The setting, characterized by stone pillars and a nearby wooden platform, suggests this performance is an integral part of a temple ritual or festival, preserving the rich musical heritage of the region.

name: Yazh Informational Plaque at Thyagaraja Temple
keywords_tags: ["Yazh", "Tamil Music", "Ancient Instruments", "Thyagaraja Temple", "Sangam Literature", "Yaal Nool", "Musical History"]
description: An informational plaque located at the Thyagaraja Temple providing a comprehensive overview of the 'Yazh', an ancient Tamil harp. The plaque details the instrument's historical prominence until the 7th century A.D. before its replacement by the Veena. It describes the Yazh as an open-stringed polyphonous instrument with a wooden resonator and a Yali-carved head. The text references its significance in Sangam literature, including the Thirukkural and Silapathikaram, and cites Swami Vipulananda's research work, 'Yaal Nool'. Additionally, it categorizes various types of Yazh, such as the Adi, Narada, and Periyazh, noting their unique string counts and characteristics.

name: Wooden Deity Carving at Thyagaraja Swamy Temple
location_text: Thyagaraja Swamy Temple, Thiruvarur, Tamil Nadu
description: An intricately carved, dark-toned wooden wall panel displayed at the Thyagaraja Swamy Temple in Thiruvarur. The carving features a multi-headed deity, possibly Brahma, rendered in deep relief within a traditional rectangular frame adorned with architectural motifs. The wood exhibits signs of age and careful polishing, highlighting the detailed craftsmanship of the deity's jewelry and garments. This piece is part of a collection of wooden carvings mounted on the temple walls, accompanied by informational signage in Tamil.

name: Vattezhuthu Inscription Educational Charts
location_text: Central University of Tamil Nadu, Thiruvarur
description: A set of three educational charts mounted on a wall at the Central University of Tamil Nadu, documenting significant Vattezhuthu inscriptions. The charts provide a comparative study of ancient epigraphy, featuring the Arachalur (300 AD), Pulankurichi (500 AD), Keelakuyilkudi (800 AD), and Suchindram (1000 AD) inscriptions. Each entry includes the original script paired with its modern Tamil transliteration, serving as a pedagogical tool for the study of Tamil linguistic history.

name: Temple Wall Paintings at Thirukkannamangai
description: A collection of traditional wall paintings located within a temple in Thirukkannamangai. The murals depict various Hindu mythological scenes, including the marriage of Lord Vishnu and Goddess Lakshmi. The artwork, some of which is over 60 years old, is displayed both in framed sections and directly on the stone walls. While some pieces retain vibrant colors, many show significant signs of age, weathering, and deterioration due to environmental exposure. The temple complex also features architectural elements such as stone pillars and painted ceilings, which contain remnants of older, more intricate mural work.

name: Thiruvarur District Overview Chart
description: A framed informational chart displayed in Thiruvarur town, providing a comprehensive statistical overview of the Thiruvarur district. The chart details key administrative and demographic information, including the district's formation date (January 1, 1997), total area, population, and a breakdown of administrative units such as taluks, revenue divisions, municipalities, and educational institutions. It serves as a public reference for local governance and district demographics.

name: Rishi Miniature Idol (11/98)
description: A miniature sculptural depiction of a Rishi (Sage) displayed in a museum in Thiruvarur. The idol is mounted on a wooden base and is identified by a plaque labeled 'முனிவர் Rishi 11/98'. The figure is shown in a traditional seated posture, representing a sage or ascetic figure common in Indian iconography.

name: Historical Philatelic and Biographical Display Collection
description: A curated display case featuring a collection of historical letters, philatelic items, and commemorative stamps. The collection is organized on white sheets, each providing a biographical summary and portrait of prominent Indian historical figures, freedom fighters, and political leaders, including Jawaharlal Nehru, B.R. Ambedkar, Indira Gandhi, and K. Kamaraj. The display also highlights significant milestones in Indian history, such as the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the Quit India Resolution, all preserved behind glass in a wooden frame.

name: Aavudayar (Shiva Lingam Base)
location_text: Central University of Tamil Nadu, Thiruvarur
keywords_tags: ["Aavudayar", "Shiva Lingam", "Stone Sculpture", "Temple Artifact", "Thiruvarur", "Central University of Tamil Nadu"]
description: This stone Aavudayar serves as the traditional base for a Shiva Lingam. It features a square-shaped foundation with a distinct, extended water outlet known as a pranalam. The center contains a circular depression designed to hold a Lingam. The artifact is currently preserved at the Central University of Tamil Nadu in Thiruvarur and is cataloged under the reference number 54/18.

name: Lakshmana Thevar I.N.A. History Sheet
keywords_tags: ["Lakshmana Thevar", "I.N.A.", "Indian National Army", "Freedom Fighter", "Tamil Nadu I.N.A. Forum", "Historical Document", "1974"]
description: A framed historical document titled 'Documents of Freedom Fighters,' issued by the Tamil Nadu I.N.A. Forum in 1974. The document serves as a 'History Sheet of I.N.A. Personnel' for Lakshmana Thevar, referencing Home Ministry letter No. 7833/73 FF. INA. It details his service as a Naik in the 8th Guerilla Regiment, his recruitment in Singapore in 1943, his participation in the freedom movement in Malaysia and Burma, and his subsequent imprisonment by the British Army. The document provides significant biographical context regarding his service and post-war repatriation.

name: Aggappaithangi (Ladle Holder)
description: An 'Aggappaithangi' (ladle holder) dating back to the 19th century A.D., currently preserved in the Thyagaraja Temple museum collection. The artifact is a long, flat wooden piece featuring five circular sections with square cutouts, specifically designed to hold the handles of ladles or spoons used in temple rituals. It is cataloged with the accession number 08/2006.

name: Aruvathimoovar Nayanmar Inscription at Thyagaraja Temple
keywords_tags: ["Thyagaraja Temple", "Aruvathimoovar Nayanmar", "Thiruthondar Thogai", "Sundaramoorthi Swamigal", "Kumaraguruparar Swamigal", "Tamil Inscription", "Thiruvarur"]
description: A stone inscription panel mounted on a wall at the Thyagaraja Temple in Thiruvarur, featuring the 'Thiruthondar Thogai' composed by the poet-saint Sundaramoorthi Swamigal. The inscription is meticulously organized into a grid of tiles, detailing the names and devotion of the Aruvathimoovar Nayanmar (the 63 Nayanmars). Below the main grid, a smaller, separate plaque contains a devotional verse by Kumaraguruparar Swamigal, which is dated 28-5-1954, indicating the installation or renovation period of this specific panel.

name: Dakshinamurthy Stone Relief Sculpture
description: A weathered stone relief sculpture of Dakshinamurthy, a form of the Hindu deity Shiva, situated on a stone wall within a temple complex in Madappuram, Thiruvarur. The sculpture depicts the deity in a traditional seated, meditative posture. The site includes architectural elements such as a gopuram and a shrine with a painted ceiling. Historical documentation identifies the piece as dating to the 9th Century A.D.

name: Singapore Coin Collection at Thyagaraja Temple
description: A small, curated display of five Singaporean coins mounted on a red square board, exhibited at the Thyagaraja Temple. The display includes a bilingual label in Tamil and English identifying the items as 'Singapore Coins'. This collection represents a modern numismatic interest within the temple complex.

name: Sri Tyagaraja Swami Birthplace
description: This site marks the birthplace of the legendary Carnatic music composer Sri Tyagaraja Swami, located in Pudhu Theru, Thiruvarur. The house is preserved as a memorial, featuring an exterior facade adorned with a statue of the saint and signage acknowledging the maintenance support provided by City Union Bank. The interior serves as a sanctified space, housing idols of the saint, informative wall inscriptions detailing his life and works, and traditional floor decorations, reflecting its status as a significant cultural landmark for music enthusiasts and devotees.

name: Archaeological Artifacts from Thyagaraja Temple
description: A collection of archaeological artifacts displayed on a white surface, reportedly recovered from the Thyagaraja Temple in Thiruvarur. The collection includes two rectangular terracotta bricks, a rounded yellowish stone, a dark textured fragment, and a curved pottery shard. While the submission was labeled as a 'Vattezhuthu Script Chart', the image contains only physical historical artifacts with no visible inscriptions.

name: Mahishasuramardini Chozha Bronze Statue
description: A significant 10th-century bronze sculpture of the goddess Mahishasuramardini, originating from Thuraikaddu in the Thanjavur District. This artifact is a prime example of Chozha period metalwork, showcasing the intricate craftsmanship and religious iconography prevalent during that era.

name: Ancient Metallic Statue at Thiyaagaraaja Swamy Temple
location_text: Thiyaagaraaja Swamy Temple, Thiruvarur, Tamil Nadu
description: This artifact consists of the lower portion of an ancient metallic statue, likely bronze, currently displayed at the Thiyaagaraaja Swamy temple in Thiruvarur. The statue features legs resting on a traditional circular lotus-shaped base (padmapitha), which is supported by a square platform. The metal exhibits a weathered, greenish-brown patina, suggesting significant age. The craftsmanship is consistent with traditional South Indian temple iconography.

The manuscript is bound with white string and is identified by a catalog label marked 'Sivapuranam 01/98'. This artifact represents traditional methods of preserving religious and literary texts in Tamil culture.

name: Ancient Lithic Artifact Collection, Thiruvarur
description: A curated collection of prehistoric stone artifacts housed in a display cabinet in Thiruvarur. The collection includes various lithic tools, such as hand-axes and scrapers, exhibiting intentional shaping and signs of wear. The artifacts display a range of natural stone colors, including grey, brown, and reddish tones, representing early human technological development in the region.

name: Rajendra Chola I Territorial Map Display
keywords_tags: ["Chola Dynasty", "Rajendra Chola I", "Historical Map", "Thyagaraja Temple", "Maritime Trade", "Thiruvarur", "Educational Display"]
description: This educational wall display, located within the Thyagaraja Temple complex, provides a visual representation of the Chola Empire's reach under Rajendra Chola I around 1030 CE. The map highlights the empire's core territories in South India, including Thanjavur and Gangaikonda Cholapuram, while detailing the extensive maritime trade routes and spheres of influence that extended across Southeast Asia, reaching regions such as Srivijaya (modern-day Palembang) and Kadaram (Kedah). The display serves as an informative resource for visitors to understand the historical geopolitical and economic dominance of the Chola dynasty.

name: Kalaignar Centenary Fruit & Vegetable Market Complex Inauguration Plaque
location_text: Old Thanjavur Road, Thiruvarur, Tamil Nadu
keywords_tags: ["Inauguration Plaque", "Thiruvarur", "Kalaignar Centenary", "Market Complex", "Tamil Nadu Government", "Urban Development"]
description: A commemorative inauguration plaque for the Kalaignar Centenary Fruit & Vegetable Market Complex, located on Old Thanjavur Road in Thiruvarur. The plaque, crafted from polished reddish-brown stone with gold-engraved Tamil text and an ornate wooden frame, marks the project's completion under the Kalaignar Urban Development Scheme (2023-2024). Inaugurated on May 11, 2025, at a cost of 1327.00 Lakhs, the plaque lists key government officials, including Chief Minister M.K. Stalin and Minister K.N. Nehru, alongside municipal representatives and the contractor, Sura Builders.

The exhibit includes mounted swords and detailed educational placards documenting 'Sangam Era Chola Country Poets' and 'Chola Era Irrigation Terms' in both Tamil and English. A notable piece in the collection is an ornate, decorative metal dagger featuring intricate engravings on its hilt and guard, providing insight into the craftsmanship of the period.

name: Pazhankala Karuvigal Collection
location_text: Central University of Tamil Nadu, Thiruvarur
description: A curated display of prehistoric stone tools housed at the Central University of Tamil Nadu. The collection features Mesolithic weapons sourced from Krishnagiri Varattanappalli, estimated to be over 200,000 years old, alongside documentation of Paleolithic weapons from the Kotralai River Valley, dating back over 1.5 million years. The exhibit serves as an educational resource on early human technology in the region.

name: International Currency Collection at Thyagaraja Temple
description: A curated display of international paper currency and a Roman medal housed within the Thyagaraja Temple in Thiruvarur. The collection includes banknotes from Brunei, Sri Lanka, the United Arab Emirates, Malaysia, Australia, Germany (Berlin), and Japan, each accompanied by bilingual labels in Tamil and English. The display serves as a point of interest for visitors, showcasing a diverse range of global currency alongside a commemorative medal.

name: Foreign Currency Collection at Thyagaraja Temple Museum
description: A curated display case located within the museum at the Thyagaraja Temple in Thiruvarur, featuring a collection of historical foreign paper currency and coins. The exhibit, labeled 'Foreign Currencies' (அயல் நாட்டு தாள் பணங்கள்), showcases banknotes from various nations including Brunei, Malaysia, Australia, Japan, Maldives, Kuwait, Singapore, Bangladesh, Saudi Arabia, and Indonesia, providing a glimpse into international numismatic history.

name: Krishna Leela Relief Carvings at Archaeological Museum Badami
description: This collection of 7th-century stone relief carvings, housed at the Archaeological Museum in Badami, Karnataka, provides a detailed narrative of the Krishna Leela. The reliefs artistically depict key mythological episodes, including the birth of Krishna, the exchange of infants between Vasudeva and Nanda, the defeat of various demons such as Putana, Dhenukasura, and Pralamba, and the lifting of the Govardhana mountain. Each panel is accompanied by a bilingual plaque in Kannada and English, offering historical and mythological context to the intricate stone work.

name: Badami Cave 3 Mural Paintings
keywords_tags: ["Badami", "Cave 3", "Mural Paintings", "Chalukya Architecture", "Archaeological Survey of India", "Conservation", "Rock-cut Temple"]
description: These mural paintings, located within the vaulted ceilings and cornices of Cave 3 at the Badami Cave Temples, represent some of the earliest surviving examples of Hindu mural art, dating back to the Chalukyan period (c. 578 CE). The paintings feature intricate geometric patterns, circular motifs, and a palette of natural pigments including ochre, red, and green. Over centuries, these artworks have suffered degradation due to environmental factors such as humidity and temperature fluctuations, as well as human interaction. Currently, the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) is conducting systematic conservation efforts to stabilize the pigments and preserve the remaining iconography for future generations.

name: Bhoothanatha Temple Rock Reliefs
description: Located on the sandstone cliff face behind the Bhoothanatha Temple in Badami, these rock-cut reliefs represent a significant archaeological feature of the region. The carvings are arranged in horizontal panels and depict a variety of Hindu deities, including Ganesha, Shiva (represented as lingas), and various forms of Vishnu such as Varaha and Narasimha. Interspersed among the divine figures are detailed architectural motifs, including miniature temple shrines (vimanas). Scholars often interpret these reliefs as prototypes or 'sketches' created by ancient sculptors to refine their techniques before undertaking larger, more complex commissions for the nearby cave temples. The site is characterized by the natural, layered geological patterns of the reddish-brown sandstone, set against the backdrop of the Agastya Tirtha lake.

name: ಕಪ್ಪೆ ಅರಭಟ್ಟನ ಶಾಸನ (Kappe Arabhatta Inscription)
description: The Kappe Arabhatta Inscription, located in Badami, is a significant 7th-century historical artifact carved onto a rock face. It is renowned for being one of the earliest examples of the 'Tripadi' poetic meter in the Kannada language. The inscription serves as a heroic poem (Veerageethe) and includes a Sanskrit verse alongside the Kannada text, providing invaluable insight into the linguistic and cultural history of the Chalukya period.

name: Kelagade Shivalaya
description: Kelagade Shivalaya, or the 'Lower Shiva Temple', is a historical stone temple situated on a rocky cliffside in Badami, Karnataka. The structure is a testament to the region's rich architectural heritage, featuring intricate stone carvings on its exterior. Currently, the temple stands as a ruined site; the sanctum sanctorum (garbhagudi) is empty, with no idol present. The site is accessible via a stone pathway and offers panoramic views of the surrounding landscape and the town of Badami below. It is often associated with the early Chalukyan architectural style, characterized by its robust stone masonry.

The inscriptions provide vital historical context, documenting the construction of the Vijayesvara (Sangamesvara), Lokesvara (Virupaksha), and Trailokesvara (Mallikarjuna) temples by the Chalukya royalty, including King Vijayaditya, Queen Lokamahadevi, and Trailokyamahadevi. It also records a land grant made during the reign of King Kirtivarma II (744-757 CE) for the maintenance of the Vijayesvara temple.

description: Sunga Chawl is a traditional Assamese delicacy prepared by slow-cooking sticky rice (bora saul) inside hollow bamboo tubes over an open fire.
